newsitem.title: USA: Concha y Toro expects '97 exports up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Concha y Toro expects '97 exports up 20 pct.

text.p: Chilean wine producer Vina Concha y Toro SA expects the volume of its 1997 exports to rise about 20 percent over last year, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
Fernando Concha Marquez de la Plata, the company's deputy chief financial officer, told Reuters Concha y Toro would focus on fast-growing foreign markets.
"We expect to continue growing in the U.S. market (and) continue growing in the European market because we're there with the right wines," he said.
Marquez, who was in New York to speak to investors, said domestic sales likely would remain flat this year. Domestic revenues totaled $42.1 million last year.
He would not give values for 1997 domestic and export sales. Marquez said the price of the wines would depend on harvests in Chile and in California.

Concha y Toro, the No 2 exporter to the U.S. market, had total exports last year of about 6.4 million gallons (40 million liters) worth $61 million. Total sales were $114.1 million, up 24 percent from 1995, and income was $15.3 million.
During a presentation, the company said it expected U.S. sales to rise to about 2.1 million cases in 1997 from 1.7 million cases last year.
Concha y Toro is forecasting a 19.2 percent increase in production this year, a five percent rise in 1998 and 5.8 percent increase in 1999, based on new plantings.
The company has budgeted about $42 million for capital expenditures over the next two years.
